Build the time ledger

tl_ledger.Rd

tl_ledger() is the centre of the package. It cuts every record's target period into disjoint half-open intervals [start, end), splitting wherever the reference state, the observation status, or any detector's response changes. Each row states what was known about that stretch of time, so every metric in the package is a sum over ledger rows and can be traced back to the seconds behind it.

Usage

tl_ledger(records, reference, predictions, observation = NULL, event = "AF",
  unknown = "unknown", missing = "unknown", time_unit = "s",
  on_warning = c("keep", "error"))

Arguments

records

Record table, usually from tl_records(): columns record, start, end, and optionally subject, fs, n_samples.

reference

Reference intervals: columns record, start, end, label. Optional episode gives a physiological episode identifier that is kept when an episode is interrupted, and optional start_sample, end_sample are checked against fs. Target time without a reference row is "unknown".

predictions

Detector responses: columns record, detector, start, end, response ("positive", "negative" or "abstain"). Optional columns: reason (why the detector abstained), issued_at (time the decision became available, used for latency).

observation

Optional input-availability intervals: columns record, start, end, status ("available" or "unavailable"), and optional reason. Uncovered time has status "unknown".

event

Reference labels that count as the target event.

unknown

Reference labels that mean the reference is unknown. NA labels are always unknown. All other labels are non-events.

missing

Meaning of target time with no prediction row: one of "unknown", "abstain", "negative", "no_input". Either one value or a named vector with one value per detector.

time_unit

Unit of all times: "ms", "s", "min" or "h". Used only to report rates per hour and errors in minutes.

on_warning

What to do with warnings found during validation: "keep" (store them as the issues attribute) or "error".

Details

Four conditions that are often merged are kept apart:

  • reference "unknown": correctness cannot be assessed;

  • response "no_input": the reference may be known, but the monitor had no input, so a prediction was impossible;

  • response "abstain": input was available and the detector declined;

  • response "negative": an actual "no event" answer that can be right or wrong.

Time not covered by any prediction row is not silently treated as negative. Its meaning comes from missing, which defaults to "unknown". A missing score is never used to infer that the device was not worn; that needs an explicit observation table.

Value

A data frame of class tl_ledger with one row per interval and detector. Columns: record, detector, start, end, duration, reference, ref_label, ref_episode, ref_reason, observation, obs_reason, response, response_source, response_reason, issued_at, conflict, ref_row, obs_row, pred_row. Attributes hold the cleaned inputs, the settings and the validation issues.

See also

tl_check(), tl_metrics(), tl_match(), tl_trace()

Examples

fx <- tl_fixture("acceptance")
led <- tl_ledger(fx$records, fx$reference, fx$predictions,
                 time_unit = "min")
led
#> <tl_ledger> 7 rows | 1 record(s) | detector(s): D | time unit: min
#>  record detector start end reference observation response    response_reason
#>    rec1        D     0  10  nonevent     unknown negative               <NA>
#>    rec1        D    10  20     event     unknown positive               <NA>
#>    rec1        D    20  40  nonevent     unknown negative               <NA>
#>    rec1        D    40  60     event     unknown  abstain low signal quality
#>    rec1        D    60  70  nonevent     unknown negative               <NA>
#>    rec1        D    70  80  nonevent     unknown positive               <NA>
#>    rec1        D    80 100  nonevent     unknown negative               <NA>
tl_check(led)
#>   record detector target ledger contiguous starts_at_target   ok
#> 1   rec1        D    100    100       TRUE             TRUE TRUE
